intro: Based on the archives of the most prominent architects and urban planners, the collection provides insight into 130 years of development in Dutch architecture and urban planning.
archiveDescription1: Nieuwe Instituut manages approximately 700 archives and collections of Dutch architects, urban planners, professional associations, and educational institutions. The collection is one of the largest in the world in the field of architecture. In addition to museum quality drawings, these archives contain sketches and preliminary designs, working drawings, business and personal correspondence, photos, models, posters, and collected clippings and published articles. The uniqueness of many archives, their artistic quality, and the added value provided by the entirety of the collection grant the Nieuwe Instituut's collection significant cultural and historical importance.
archiveDescription2: In the mid-19th century, coinciding with the founding of the professional association Maatschappij tot Bevordering der Bouwkunst (Society for the Promotion of Architecture), the education of architects in the modern sence started taking shape. From that moment onwards, architectural archives were established. The archives of the firm of P.J.H. Cuypers and his son J.Th. Cuypers are among the important collection pieces from the 19th century. The collection's emphasis is on the period 1900-1940, with archives from H.P. Berlage, K.P.C. de Bazel, W. Kromhout, M. de Klerk, J.J.P. Oud, W.M. Dudok, J. Duiker, J.A. Brinkman and L.C. van der Vlugt, T. van Doesburg, H. Th. Wijdeveld, G. Th. Rietveld, and C. van Eesteren. The Nieuwe Bouwen movement is a key focus within this collection. The post-war reconstruction period (1940-1965) is well documented with the archives of J.H. van den Broek and J.B. Bakema, H. Maaskant, and W. Wissing. More recent archives include those of Herman Hertzberger, Sjoerd Soeters, Alberts and Van Huut and OMA.
archiveDescription3: The archives of institutions and educational programs in the field of architecture also form an important part of the collection, such as the Maatschappij tot Bevordering der Bouwkunst, Bond van Nederlandse Architecten (BNA), NIROV, and the Academy of Architecture Amsterdam. This also applies to the results of significant competitions and exhibitions. Examples include the competitions for the Amsterdam town hall in 1936 and 1967, the competition for the Stock Exchange in Rotterdam, an exhibition like "Nederland bouwt in Baksteen" (The Netherlands Builds in Brick) (1941), and the photo panels of the Exhibition Council (1925-1935).
archiveDescription4: The National Collection for Dutch Architecture and Urban Planning contains both analog and born-digital material; archival material originally produced in digital format. Archives which contain born-digital material are, amongst others, the archives of MVRDV and Michael van Gessel. The e-depot includes more than 5 TB of data with over 1,000,000 files ranging from 2D architectural drawings and 3D models to images, videos, animations, renderings, and computer code. The technological shift in design practice from analog to digital and the expected growth of the born-digital collection is a significant reason for the Nieuwe Instituut to invest time and resources in the preservation and storage of digital files.
libraryDescription1: Nieuwe Instituut collects and manages publications on Dutch and international architecture, urban planning, and related subjects such as housing, spatial planning, landscape architecture, and interior architecture. The focus of the collection is on modern architecture (from the 19th century onwards). In addition to architecture and urban planning, Nieuwe Instituut also collects information on art, photography, digital culture, design, and societal trends like globalization, media, the network society, and the entertainment industry. With this, Nieuwe Instituut aims to follow developments that influence the organization of the space around us in a broad perspective.
libraryDescription2: The library collection consists of approximately 72,500 books and brochures and 1,300 journal titles from both domestic and international sources, of which 40 are current subscriptions. The audiovisual collection contains about 550 videotapes, DVDs, CDs, and cassette tapes. Additionally, Nieuwe Instituut possesses a collection of rare books and magazines from the 20th century and folios from the 18th and 19th centuries.
